chunks: Abdul Wahid ibn Muhammad ibn Ubdoos al-Naysaboori al-Attar narrated in Naysaboor in the month of Sha'ban in the year 352 A.H. that Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutaybah al-Naysaboori narrated from Fadl ibn Shadan who said, 'I heard Imam Al-Ridha (peace be upon him) say:'

When God the Almighty ordered Abraham (peace be upon him) to sacrifice the sheep He sent down in place of his son Ishmael, Abraham wished that he had sacrificed his son Ishmael with his own hand, and that he had not been ordered to sacrifice the sheep in his place, so that the feeling that returns to the heart of a father who sacrifices his dearest son with his own hand would return to his heart, and thus he would deserve the highest ranks of reward for calamities.

Then God the Almighty revealed to him, 'O Abraham! Who is My dearest creature in your eyes?' He said, 'O my Lord! You have not created anyone who is dearer to me than your friend Muhammad.' Then God revealed to him, 'Is he dearer to you or are you dearer to yourself?' He said, 'No, he is dearer to me than myself.' He said, 'Is his child dearer to you or your child?' He said, 'His child.'

He said, 'Will the oppressive beheading of his child by his enemies hurt you more, or the beheading of your child by your hand in My obedience?' He said, 'O my Lord, of course, the beheading of his child by his enemies will hurt me more.'

He said, 'O Abraham! A group of people who claim to be from the nation of Muhammad will slaughter his son Hussein after him oppressively and aggressively, just as the sheep is slaughtered, and they will incur My wrath thereby.' Abraham became distressed by this, his heart ached, and he began to weep.

Then God the Almighty revealed to him, 'O Abraham! I have accepted your distress over your son Ishmael had you sacrificed him with your hand, as your distress over Hussein and his killing, and I have obligated for you the highest ranks of reward for calamities.'
And that is the word of God the Almighty: 'And We ransomed him with a momentous sacrifice.'
And there is no power nor any strength but in God.
ai.seo_question: How does the sacrifice of Prophet Ibrahim's son relate to the martyrdom of Imam Hussein according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Imam Al-Ridha elucidates the theological depth of Surah As-Saffat 107 by framing the near-sacrifice of Ishmael as a prelude to the martyrdom of Imam Hussein. The text highlights a divine comparison where Abraham’s grief over Hussein’s unjust death by enemies is deemed more profound than the obedience of slaughtering his son, thereby elevating the Ahl al-Bayt's suffering to a status of supreme reward. This interpretation underscores the Shia view that the trials of the Imams are not merely historical events but pivotal cosmic realities that validate prophetic lineage and divine mercy.
